Rachel / Monica —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed BlueWing’s numbers and sketched three options (attached spreadsheet) with trade-offs. Summary below:

Option A — Short-term soft reserve (recommended if sales needs a hard promise)
- Reserve: 8 x A100-equivalent slots for 30 days starting 2027-08-10
- Delivery: immediate reservation, can be rebalanced by infra after 14 days if a higher-priority committed deal emerges
- Cost: premium 1.6x for short-term reserve + one-time reconfiguration fee
- Risk: reduces burst availability for the share pool; may cause 5–10% degradation in peak headroom for top-tier hosted customers

Option B — Burst + PV2 buffer (lower risk)
- No hard reservation; provide prioritized burst credits (auto-burst to dedicated when capacity exists) and a 48-hour SLA to spin up reserved nodes if commit executes
- Cost: lower (1.1x), but no guarantee of capacity during cluster saturation
- Risk: possible throttling on very high concurrency days; better for uncertain/early-stage volume

Option C — Commit-first (safest for infra predictability)
- Require signed SOW + 90-day commit to provision dedicated capacity (12 x A100-eq)
- Cost: standard reserved pricing (no premium); lowest infra risk
- Risk: may lose the deal if BlueWing cannot sign quickly

Operational notes:
- We can implement a short-term reserve with a rollback policy: if a higher-priority committed allocation is requested, we surface 48 hours notice and present alternate routes (burst, traffic shaping, model variant fallback).
- For fairness, we should track short-term reserves as an internal ledger item that counts against sales’ monthly allocation budget.

I attached gpu-allocation-options.xlsx with throughput estimates, latency impact, and a simple priority ledger template.

Attachments: gpu-allocation-options.xlsx (XLSX)

Please confirm which option you want to propose to Jamie. If sales wants Option A, we can lock the reservation pending a 25% good-faith deposit or signed PO.
